correctness.rationale: The n natural-basis squares span E² because all cross products vanish, and perfection makes these n vectors a basis. Thus the coefficients in g(e_i)g(e_j)=0 force disjoint supports for the columns of every genuine automorphism g, which is monomial by invertibility. Interpolation at pairs of natural-basis elements shows the nonzero images T(e_i)=c_i e_{σ(i)} occupy distinct coordinates. For any x and i, the witness for (e_i,x) has exactly one entry in row σ(i), namely c_i in column i, so that row of T(x) is forced to be c_i x_i. This reconstructs the entire invertible linear map with no field-size hypothesis. The witnesses at (e_i,e_i²) give the diagonal product constraints, and disjoint image coordinates give all off-diagonal ones. Bilinearity completes multiplicativity; no polarization or division by 2 is used. The zero-dimensional case is automatic. Independent enumeration using full multiplication tables and all 256 set maps for each of the six invertible F₂ structure matrices of dimension two confirms the equality there (eight ordinary automorphisms counted across the six algebras).
residual_risks: Finite enumeration corroborates only that small characteristic-two case. The argument uses finite dimension and independence of the squares, not arbitrary natural bases in nonperfect algebras.

evidence: Corollary 2.5 establishes monomiality of actual automorphisms over arbitrary fields. Theorem 5.4 concerns linear local automorphisms of maximal-index nilpotent evolution algebras in characteristic zero, with separate results about two-local derivations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The ordinary automorphism result describes the matching maps, not the arbitrary set map being matched; the nilpotent linear local theorem neither has the relevant algebra class nor removes linearity and characteristic restrictions.

evidence: Monomiality enables recovery of the coordinates, but even a group of permutation matrices need not be 2-closed in its vector action: for A_n on F₂^n with n≥5, two bit vectors color the positions by only four pairs, so their joint stabilizer in S_n contains a transposition. Every odd coordinate permutation is then two-local for the A_n action. In the theorem the square-product witnesses supply actual membership in the algebra automorphism group.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither monomiality nor generic orbit formalism mechanically gives the rigidity. The algebra-specific diagonal constraints, compatible with all characteristics, are decisive.

evidence: On a finite underlying vector space the statement is 2-closedness in the action on all vectors. The 2-closure definition in Chen–Ren is preservation of ordered-pair orbits. The survey asks about related locality questions but does not state the present rigidity result in the inspected passage.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The finite action reformulation is exact, but is not a theorem asserting that this action is 2-closed. The argument also handles arbitrary infinite fields without appealing to finite bijectivity.

originality.rationale: The credited result is arbitrary-map two-point rigidity for all finite-dimensional perfect evolution algebras over all fields, not monomiality of ordinary automorphisms. The closest source supplying monomiality does not give the simultaneous coordinate and square interpolation argument that upgrades pointwise witnesses to one multiplicative map.
residual_risks: Bounded comparison, not a priority determination; broader results on 2-closed algebraic actions may have been missed.

value.rationale: Perfect evolution algebras form a natural class with constrained but potentially varied automorphism groups. It is useful to know that two simultaneous evaluations already rule out every nonlinear or nonglobal interpolant, uniformly including the smallest fields and characteristic two. This is a class-wide rigidity result, and the pair-of-squares mechanism identifies why the known monomial structure is enough in the algebraic action but not for arbitrary monomial groups.
residual_risks: No assertion about one-point local maps, two-local derivations, or nonperfect algebras.
